took: Continued this session past CYC-0101: session_cap.py --check reported this session has written 1 receipt against a cap of 2 and must not stop, and continuity.py --check kept refusing an idle stop while 155 ready items sat in the queue. Re-scored, took the next top item, AUT-219 (172.0, RT-EARLY-PALLIATIVE's remaining_validation item 1). Skipped a re-check of cadence.py (its 8h gate is for the driver Routine's fire spacing, not for a second cycle inside an already-running session -- matching the CYC-0099/CYC-0100 precedent) but re-ran health.py --check, which cleared.
what_changed: AUT-219's own text claimed the trial set was 'already retrieved', but the source manuscript it points at (emc-mortality-mechanisms.md) explicitly said the palliative-care queries were still 'AWAITING' results -- an unverified premise, per CLAUDE.md §0's 'a claim that needs evidence, and it is usually wrong', that turned out to be PARTLY wrong: the probe file (emc-mortality-probe.json) DID already carry 25 retrieved hits under 'early_palliative_care_survival', but none were the landmark RCT the route's rationale implicitly assumed (Temel et al. 2010) or its replications -- the existing retrieval was recent reviews/observational studies, not the RCT evidence base the route actually needed. Dispatched a fresh, targeted fetch-literature.yml run (33823172816, control PMID 20818875 matched) and read: Temel et al. 2010 (NEJM, PMID 20818875, metastatic NSCLC n=151, median OS 11.6 vs 8.9 months p=0.02); Allende et al. 2024/PACO (Oncologist, PMID 38558247, Mexico/LMIC NSCLC n=146, HR 1.5 [1.04-2.3] p=.030) -- an independent replication in a different health system; Chen et al. 2023 (Front Oncol, PMID 37781179, China NSCLC n=140, HR 0.19 [0.04-0.85] p=0.029) -- a second independent replication; and Kochovska et al. 2020 (Transl Lung Cancer Res, PMID 32953543, systematic review/meta-analysis) giving the 2020 evidence-base context (only 2 studies with survival data then, one of them a timing-not-presence comparison). All three RCTs are NSCLC, months-scale survival -- the route's central transfer question to EMC's decade-scale natural history is answered by none of them and stays explicitly open. A title-level search of the 388-paper retrieved corpus found no sarcoma-specific palliative-care trial (one coincidental, unrelated hit). Registered EV-TEMEL-2010, EV-PACO-2024, EV-CHEN-2023-CEPC, EV-KOCHOVSKA-2020 in systems/graph/evidence.json. Wrote the finding into RT-EARLY-PALLIATIVE's rationale/supporting_evidence/remaining_unknowns/readiness/next in systems/graph/routes.json; required_validation item 1 is answered (item 2, a sarcoma-specific trial, stays blocked on BLK-NO-WET-LAB). Regenerated systems/views/.
